title: Variation in proteome landscape in human pancreatic islets
projectDescription: Human pancreatic islets were collected from cadavic donors. Left our islets from 16 donors not used for transpantation were lysed and whole protein extract were collected. 16 samples were used to be able to assess variations in the proteome landscape between donors.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Proteins were digested to peptides before desalting and drying. The peptides were combined with TMTpro16 reagents and concentrated to near dryness followed by desalting via C18 solid phase extraction. The pooled labeled peptide samples were fractionated using basic pH reversedphase fractionation using a Agilet 300Extend C18 column. The peptide mixture was factionated into 96 fractions, which were consolidated into 24 super-fractions. Each pf the 12 non-adjacent fractions were analysed on an Orbitrap Eclipse mass spectometer.
dataProcessingProtocol: Mass spectra were processed using a Comet-based in-house softare pipeline (Huttlin, Jedrychowki et al. 2010)and spectra were converted to mzxml using a modifived version of ReAdW.exe. Database searhing included all entries from the human Uniprot database (March 2021). Peptide-spectrum matches (PSMs) were adjusted to a 1% FDR. PSM filtering was poerformed using a linear djscriminant analysis. Proteins were quantified by summing reporter ino counts across all matching PSMs usin in-house software (Huttlin, Jedrychowki et al. 2010.
